pages.mainText: Home / Image tools / Background Remover Image tools Background Remover Drop in a photo and this tool cuts the subject out from its background automatically, using a small machine-learning model that runs entirely on your device. The image is never uploaded anywhere, which makes this suitable for photos you'd rather not send to a third-party server. Remove a photo's background Click to choose an image or drag and drop it here JPG, PNG, or WebP Choose an image The first use downloads about 52 MB once, then your browser can reuse it. Download PNG Inspect an actual removal result The recorded 480 × 360 synthetic mug output retains large beige areas above the rim and around the handle, together with smaller edge remnants. Transparent pixels do not make it a clean cutout. Inspect the complete result; use a manual editor or another source if fragments remain. Input or check Expected result or decision Source A solid mug against a pale illustrated background. Result Some pixels become transparent, but substantial background areas remain. The recorded result needs manual cleanup. Decision Check on light and dark backgrounds; use a manual editor if the retained pixels matter. Download the licensed photograph · Inspect its actual model output · Photograph source and CC0 license Actual synthetic result: large background fragments remain; manual cleanup is needed. Download the test input · Inspect the transparent PNG result How it works When you choose a file, a compact background-segmentation model loads in your browser (only once per visit). The model identifies the main subject and produces a version of the image with a transparent background. Both the original and the result are shown side by side so you can compare before downloading. The output downloads as a PNG, which supports transparency, so you can drop it straight onto a new background. Common uses Cutting out a product photo for a listing or catalog. Preparing a headshot for a resume or profile without a distracting background. Making a transparent sticker-style image from a photo for a presentation or design. Your privacy matters here: check the FAQ below for exactly what happens to anything you enter into this tool. Improve the edges Use a sharp photograph with a clearly separated subject. Fine hair, transparent objects and shadows can be difficult. The first run downloads a model; later runs can reuse browser-cached model files. A practical walkthrough Choose a product photograph with a clear subject, remove its background, then download the transparent result. Inspect fine edges, hair, and transparent objects against both light and dark backgrounds before publishing. Compare the original and result previews, then download the transparent PNG. Keep your original image. Tips for a reliable result The first run downloads model assets and can take longer. A smaller source image can help on devices with limited memory. What to use next These tools open separately; inputs are not transferred. PDF tools Image to PDF Converter Turn JPG, PNG, or WebP images into ordered pages in one downloadable PDF. Open tool → Generators Color Palette Generator Generate a five-color palette for design work, with the option to lock colors you like. Open tool → Generators QR Code Generator Turn any link or short message into a scannable QR code you can download as an image. Open tool → Developer tools Base64 Encoder & Decoder Convert text to Base64 and back, entirely in your browser. Open tool → Questions and troubleshooting Does my photo get uploaded anywhere? No. Processing happens locally using your device's own processing power, so the image never leaves your browser. Why does the first image take longer than the second? The first run downloads and initializes the small ML model used for segmentation. After that, it stays cached for the rest of your visit. What image formats are supported? JPG, PNG, and WebP work well. Very large images may take longer to process on slower devices. Why does the edge of my subject look slightly rough? Automatic segmentation works best with a clear subject and reasonable contrast against the background. Busy backgrounds or fine detail like loose hair can produce a less clean edge. When image processing stalls Allow the model resources to finish loading and keep the tab open during processing. If the browser runs out of memory, retry with a smaller supported image and fewer open tabs. For missed hair, glass, or thin edges, improve the source photo or use an editor with manual selection. Why does the first image take longer? The browser loads the image-processing model and runtime before it can remove a background. Wait for the status message and keep the tab open. A smaller image can help a device with limited memory. Will every edge be perfect? No. Hair, glass, shadows, and a subject that blends into the background can produce rough edges. Inspect the transparent output at full size and retain the original for manual corrections. pages.title: Base64 Encoder & Decoder
pages.mainText: Home / Developer tools / Base64 Encoder & Decoder Developer tools Base64 Encoder & Decoder Encode UTF-8 text as standard Base64, or decode a standard Base64 value back to text. This tool does not accept binary files. URL-safe Base64 uses a different alphabet; use the JWT Decoder for JWT header and payload sections. Encode or decode Base64 Input Encode Decode Copy result Check a text round trip This tool encodes UTF-8 text using standard Base64. Standard Base64 can include +, /, and =; it is not automatically safe as an unescaped URL parameter. Base64url uses a different alphabet. Neither form encrypts its contents. Input or check Expected result or decision Hello SGVsbG8= café Y2Fmw6k= Decode either output The original text returns; arbitrary binary files are outside this text-only tool. UTF-8 text: café 🙂 Y2Fmw6kg8J+Zgg== → decoding returns café 🙂 exactly, including one space. Try this sample How it works Paste plain text and click encode to get its Base64 representation. Paste a Base64 string and click decode to recover the original text. Unicode text, including accented characters and emoji, is handled correctly in both directions. Common uses Embedding a small piece of data inside a URL or config value. Decoding a Base64-encoded token or payload while debugging an API. Preparing text for systems that only accept plain ASCII characters. Your privacy matters here: check the FAQ below for exactly what happens to anything you enter into this tool. Try a Unicode round trip Encode a short sentence containing an emoji, then decode the result. You should get the original sentence back. Base64 is an encoding, not encryption: anyone with the output can decode it. A practical walkthrough Encode a short test string such as Hello, then decode the output to check that it returns the original text. Preserve padding and character case when copying encoded data between systems. Use Copy to copy the output, and test the reverse operation to check that your text is preserved. Tips for a reliable result Base64 is an encoding, not encryption. Anyone who receives the encoded value can decode it; do not use it to hide credentials. What to use next These tools open separately; inputs are not transferred. Developer tools URL Encoder & Decoder Encode text for a URL or decode percent-encoded values safely. Open tool → Developer tools JWT Decoder Inspect a JWT header and payload without uploading the token. Open tool → Developer tools Hash Generator Generate SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 hashes from UTF-8 text. Open tool → Developer tools CSV to JSON Converter Convert quoted CSV data into JSON arrays or objects locally. Open tool → Questions and troubleshooting Is Base64 encryption? No. Base64 is an encoding, not encryption — anyone can decode it back to the original text. Don't use it to protect sensitive information. Why did decoding fail? The input wasn't valid Base64, often because of extra whitespace, line breaks, or characters outside the Base64 alphabet. Does this work with files, not just text? This tool handles text input and output. For encoding files, a dedicated file-to-Base64 tool is a better fit. When Base64 decoding fails Check that the input is complete standard Base64 rather than a Base64url token segment or a copied filename. Arbitrary binary bytes may not decode as UTF-8 text. Use the JWT Decoder for token inspection and a file-capable decoder for binary documents. Can Base64 protect confidential text? No. It is a reversible representation, not encryption. Do not share a Base64 value if the original text contains a secret. Why does a JWT section fail in a standard Base64 decoder? JWTs use Base64URL, which differs in its alphabet and padding conventions. Use the JWT Decoder for token headers and payloads; decoding does not verify their authenticity. Format or validate JSON Paste your JSON Format Minify Copy result Compare valid syntax and intended data Use the sample, then choose Format or Minify. Minify {"id":1,"id":2} {"id":2}; the earlier duplicate value is discarded. Minify {"id":9007199254740993} {"id":9007199254740992}; quote the identifier in the source to preserve its digits. No. Formatting and validation both run entirely in your browser using the JavaScript engine's built-in JSON parser. What does an 'invalid JSON' error mean? It means the parser hit something that isn't valid JSON syntax, commonly a trailing comma, an unquoted key, or a missing bracket. The error message names the position where parsing failed. Does this support JSON5 or JSONC (with comments)? No, only standard JSON. Comments and trailing commas need to be removed first. When JSON parsing fails Inspect the reported error and the surrounding syntax. Replace single-quoted keys, remove trailing commas, and use lowercase true, false, and null. Comments require a different format such as JSONC; this formatter accepts standard JSON. Keep the original for duplicate keys and large-number checks. Does valid JSON mean my configuration is correct? No. Syntax validation confirms the data can be parsed. It does not check your application's schema, required fields, permissions, or business rules. Can formatting change numbers or duplicate properties? Parsing and re-serializing JSON can lose duplicate property names and precision for numbers beyond JavaScript's safe integer range. No finite random identifier can offer an absolute guarantee, but version 4 UUIDs have 122 random bits, making accidental collisions extraordinarily unlikely when generated correctly. Are they generated securely? Yes. The tool uses crypto.randomUUID when available and a crypto.getRandomValues fallback with RFC 4122 version and variant bits. How is reading time calculated? Word count divided by 200 words per minute, rounded up to the nearest minute. Does it count numbers and punctuation as words? Numbers are counted as words if they're separated by spaces. Punctuation attached to a word doesn't count separately. When a count differs from another app Compare the exact final text, including whitespace and line breaks. The receiving form's counting rule determines its submission limit. Why does another editor show a different count? Word boundaries vary between applications, particularly for punctuation, hyphenated words, and languages without spaces. Use the destination platform's count when a submission has a strict limit. Are character limits the same everywhere? No. Platforms can count line breaks, spaces, emoji, and Unicode characters differently. Check the final text in the place where it will be submitted.
